paragraphs: All creation traces back to the creator— originally one, now separated, each yearning for reunion. Creation longs to return to its source; the creator longs to be present with creation. This mutual yearning—woven into the fabric of existence—pulls both toward restored oneness.

Plotinus articulates one side: all things proceed from “the One” and naturally turn back toward the One [11]. Laozi echoes this from the East: “Flourishing as they do, each creature returns to its root” [12]. Heschel articulates the other side: it is not only humanity that seeks the divine, but the divine that seeks humanity [13]. The creator extends outward; creation yearns inward. Both movements arise from the same root: the pull of original unity seeking to restore itself.
